grand_strategy.reading: The Gambia is small and dependent: its post-2017 order rests on Senegal, and its best-known foreign instrument is the ICJ case against Myanmar, which gives a small state a voice in The Hague. The older diplomacy (the 2016 switch from Taipei to Beijing, and the 2017-2018 Commonwealth return) is sourced here only at the level of the event, not of the lasting ties. Not verified in this pass, and therefore not in the card: the 2026 presidential election and the third-term question, the TRRC and Jammeh's legacy, the EU and migration deals, Turkey and the Gulf, ECOWAS and the ECOMIG force, and the Senegal ferry and bridge.

stances.note: Mirror of the SEN card's reading (same source, same URL). Senegal sent troops in January 2017 to back Adama Barrow, which is cooperation, not alignment: partner is our reading (C). Bond kin is our reading: shared faith and language and the 1981-89 Senegambia confederation, taken from the Wikipedia index (tier 4, pointer only). Trend stable is a default. Gaps: no 2022-26 source on Gambia-Senegal relations was reached in this pass; the Casamance question, the ferry and the bridge are unsourced.

stances.note: The Gambia sought to rejoin the Commonwealth from February 2017 and applied formally in January 2018; the UK said it was 'very pleased' (BBC). Partner is our reading of a relation with no alliance: cooperation on Commonwealth terms. Bond affinity is our reading (C): the Commonwealth return is an expression of sympathy with a former colonial power, not kinship. Trend warming is our reading of the 2017-2018 return; no source after 2018 was reached. Gap: the UK migration deals of 2022-26 are not sourced.
